Subject: Sharp p95/p99 jump for Hosted API from our US users

Marissa —

We're seeing a sudden jump in response times from our integration with Redwood's Hosted API starting at ~08:55 PT. p95 has gone from ~420ms to ~1.2s and p99 is spiking above 2s. Error rate is steady but throughput is fine. This is affecting BrightBeam's search UX for users in West Coast (US-WEST region).

Sample request-id: rb-req-7782431, trace: 7a9f3d. Our SREs ran traceroutes and a subset of requests are getting routed via eu-west hop which adds ~400ms RTT. We're attaching a screenshot from our monitoring (bb_latency_chart.png).

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (peering, egress, routing rules)? This is impacting our SLAs — we need a root cause and ETA to fix.

— Samir

Quick update from infra: we reproduced the symptom. A subset of requests originating from BrightBeam's us-west IP ranges were being NATed through an eu-west egress node due to a recent peering preference change pushed yesterday during a maintenance window.

Evidence:
- Router logs show BGP preference override for prefix 54.192.0.0/18 -> next-hop eu-west-1 (seen at 08:49 PT).
- Traces for rb-req-7782431 show an extra 360–420ms RTT when the eu hop is taken.
- Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/hosted/latency?panelId=5 (live).

Impact: p95 across BrightBeam's traffic rose 2–3x for ~35% of their requests. No token/data leakage; this is a network routing policy issue.

Immediate mitigation steps executed:
1) Rolled back the peering preference change for the affected prefixes (SUP-3245).
2) Added a temporary routing rule to prefer local US egress for known BrightBeam prefixes.
3) Warmed up a short-lived cache on the us-west POP to avoid cache-miss penalties while connections re-establish.

Status: the rollback is complete, but BGP convergence is ~10–20 minutes for all edge nodes. I'll keep this thread updated.

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sean — looping you in because BrightBeam is expressing SLA impact and wants an ETA plus potential credit. Rishi's found a peering preference regression that routed some traffic through eu-west adding ~400ms. We're already rolling back and applying a temporary US-e2e preference.

- Please approve up to a one-month pro-rata credit (up to 10%) for this incident pending a postmortem.
- If you want to join the call with BrightBeam's CTO at 11:30 PT, I'll schedule and send dial-in.

Customer impact: BrightBeam production search latency for a subset of users (us-west) was degraded starting ~08:49 PT; total customer-facing errors minimal but UX degraded. Rishi estimates normal p95 restored within ~30–40 minutes of the rollback finishing.

I'll capture a timeline and provide a postmortem link once complete.

Thanks —
Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Resolution: BrightBeam routing rollback complete — p95 restored

Final update —

Timeline summary:
- 08:49 PT: BGP preference change caused affected BrightBeam prefixes to take eu-west egress (observed spike).
- 09:00 PT: BrightBeam alert and escalation to Redwood.
- 09:10–10:00 PT: Infra triage, rollback applied to peering preferences and temporary US-e2e rule added.
- 10:12 PT: Majority of routes converged; observing p95 trending back to baseline.
- 10:35 PT: All POPs converged; p95 and p99 back within BrightBeam's SLA targets.
- 11:30 PT: Exec call with BrightBeam CTO — confirmed user experience restored.
- 16:05 PT: Post-incident runbook updated and reroute-config.diff attached; 10% pro-rata credit issued and noted in HubSpot deal BB-4821.

Attachments: reroute-config.diff, invoice_credit_note.pdf

Action items:
- Ops: add automated guardrail to prevent peering preference changes for customer prefixes without an approval flow (SUP-3246).
- Product: review how regional egress preferences are surfaced in the console (PM follow-up).
- CS (Marissa): send formal apology + credit note to BrightBeam and confirm postmortem distribution.

Customer feedback: BrightBeam acknowledged resolution and appreciated the fast rollback; they requested a short postmortem and better tooling to flag region-steering changes.

Rishi
